class.name: LandscapeFoliage3D
class.brief_description: Foliage (trees, bushes, grass, rocks...) painted on a [Landscape3D].
class.description: Instances of [LandscapeFoliageType]s placed on the terrain of a [Landscape3D] ancestor, similar to foliage in Unreal Engine. In the editor, they are painted in the Foliage tab of the Landscape dock (paint, erase, single instance, reapply, fill), with undo and redo. Instances are stored in the space of the landscape and sorted into square cells ([member chunk_size]): - each cell is drawn with one [MultiMesh] per level of detail, with the bounds of the cell, so cells are frustum and occlusion culled independently by every camera. The cells that the terrain hides from the camera of the landscape only draw their shadows ([member terrain_occlusion_culling]). While the level of detail of the landscape is frozen ([member Landscape3D.freeze_lod]), the cells out of the view of its camera are hidden too, like the patches of the landscape; - the level of detail of each instance is chosen from its distance to the camera of the landscape (see [member Landscape3D.lod_camera_path]). Cells entirely within one level are drawn with that level as a whole and aren't updated until they leave it; cells crossing a level or cull distance are sorted per instance, with hysteresis ([member LandscapeFoliageType.lod_transition]), and only the levels whose instances changed are uploaded; - cells beyond the cull distance have no rendering resources; the updates are limited to a time budget per frame, cells in the view of the camera first, then the nearest ones. With [member gpu_indirect] (Forward+ and Mobile renderers), the instances around the camera are culled and sorted per level of detail on the GPU instead, straight into indirect [MultiMesh]es: no per-cell draw calls, per-instance culling by the view frustum, the terrain and the occlusion buffer of every camera, no CPU work when the camera moves. Instances can be saved to a [LandscapeFoliageData] file ([member data], [code].lfdata[/code]) instead of the scene: then only the cells within the cull distance of the camera and of the [StreamingSource3D]s are loaded (in the background, through [WorldStreaming]), and the others are released within a memory budget ([member ProjectSettings.rendering/landscape/streaming/foliage_cache_size_mb]). The per-instance random value [code]INSTANCE_CUSTOM.x[/code] (between [code]0[/code] and [code]1[/code]) can be used by shaders for variations. When the terrain is sculpted (in the editor or at runtime), instances follow it ([member follow_terrain]). [b]Note:[/b] The transform of this node is ignored: instances are placed in the space of the landscape and move with it.

method.name: add_foliage_type
method.description: Adds a foliage type without instances and returns its index.

method.name: add_instance
method.description: Adds an instance of the type [param type_index] with a global transform. It keeps its height above the ground when the terrain changes.

method.name: add_instances
method.description: Adds instances of the type [param type_index] with global transforms.

method.name: clear
method.description: Removes all instances of the type [param type_index] (of all types when negative).

method.name: erase
method.description: Removes random instances of the type [param type_index] in a horizontal circle (global center, radius in meters) until [param density_scale] times the density of the type is left in it ([code]0[/code]: all of them). A negative type index erases every type. Returns the number of removed instances.

method.name: estimate_fill_count
method.description: Returns the number of instances [method fill] would place on the whole landscape without filters (the density of the type times the area of the landscape).

method.name: fill
method.description: Places the type [param type_index] everywhere its filters allow it, at its density, in a rect of the landscape space (the whole landscape when empty). Existing instances count towards the density. Returns the number of new instances.

method.name: find_foliage_type
method.description: Returns the index of a foliage type, or [code]-1[/code].

method.name: force_update
method.description: Rebuilds the rendering of all cells.

method.name: get_foliage_type
method.description: Returns the foliage type at [param index].

method.name: get_foliage_type_count
method.description: Returns the number of foliage types.

method.name: get_instance_count
method.description: Returns the number of instances of the type [param type_index] (of all types when negative).

method.name: get_instance_transforms
method.description: Returns the global transforms of the instances of the type [param type_index], optionally only those inside a global [AABB].

method.name: get_instances_in_radius
method.description: Returns the global transforms of the instances of the type [param type_index] in a horizontal circle.

method.name: get_instances_in_rect
method.description: Returns the instances of the type [param type_index] in a rect of the landscape space, as raw data ([constant INSTANCE_FLOATS] floats per instance). Used by the undo and redo of the editor tools, with [method set_instances_in_rect].

method.name: get_statistics
method.description: Returns statistics about the instances and their rendering: [code]types[/code], [code]instances[/code], [code]cells[/code], [code]cells_rendered[/code] (cells with rendering resources, or uploaded to the GPU), [code]cells_mixed[/code] (cells sorted per instance), [code]cells_out_of_view[/code] (cells hidden out of the frozen view of the camera, see [member Landscape3D.freeze_lod]), [code]cells_hidden_by_terrain[/code] (see [member terrain_occlusion_culling]), [code]batches[/code] (drawn multimeshes), [code]instances_drawn[/code], [code]update_usec[/code] and [code]updated_cells[/code] (last update of the levels of detail), [code]debug_bounds[/code] (cells whose bounds are drawn by [member debug_view]). GPU indirect rendering: [code skip-lint]gpu_indirect[/code] (whether it is active), [code]gpu_instances[/code] (instances uploaded to the GPU), [code]gpu_shadow_instances_drawn[/code], [code]gpu_frustum_culled[/code], [code]gpu_terrain_culled[/code] and [code]gpu_occlusion_culled[/code] (instances culled by the view frustum, by the terrain and by the occlusion buffer for the last camera drawn), [code]gpu_dropped[/code] (instances not drawn because of [member gpu_max_instances]) and [code]gpu_memory[/code] (bytes). With the GPU, [code]instances_drawn[/code] counts the visible instances of the last camera drawn (read back a few frames later). Streaming: [code]streamed[/code], [code]cells_loaded[/code], [code]cells_loading[/code], [code]loaded_memory[/code] (bytes of the loaded cells) and [code]data_memory[/code] (bytes kept by [member data], see [method LandscapeFoliageData.get_memory_usage]).

method.name: get_type_data
method.description: Returns the instances of the type [param type_index] compressed, as stored in [member instance_data].

method.name: is_gpu_indirect_active
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the instances are culled on the GPU: [member gpu_indirect] is enabled, the renderer supports it (see [method is_gpu_indirect_supported]) and the node is in the scene tree.

method.name: is_gpu_indirect_supported
method.description: Returns [code]true[/code] if the renderer supports [member gpu_indirect] (Forward+ and Mobile, not Compatibility nor headless).

method.name: load_all_cells
method.description: Loads every cell of the streamed [member data] now, e.g. before processing all the instances. The cells far from the camera are released again by the next streaming updates. Methods reading or editing instances load the cells they need by themselves.

method.name: move_foliage_type
method.description: Moves the foliage type at index [param from] (with its instances) to index [param to].

method.name: paint
method.description: Adds instances of the type [param type_index] in a horizontal circle (global center, radius in meters) until [param density_scale] times its density is reached where its filters allow it. Repeated calls at the same place don't add more. Returns the number of new instances.

method.name: place_instance
method.description: Places one instance of the type [param type_index] on the ground below a global position, with the placement settings of the type (without its filters). Returns [code]false[/code] outside of the landscape.

method.name: reapply
method.description: Applies the current placement settings (scale, rotation, alignment, offset) and filters of the type [param type_index] to its instances in a horizontal circle: instances that don't match the filters anymore are removed. Returns the number of changed or removed instances.

method.name: remove_foliage_type
method.description: Removes the foliage type at [param index] and its instances.

method.name: remove_instances_in_radius
method.description: Removes the instances of the type [param type_index] in a horizontal circle (a negative type index removes all types). Returns the number of removed instances.

method.name: save_to_data_file
method.description: Saves every instance to a [LandscapeFoliageData] file at [param path] ([code].lfdata[/code]) and streams the instances from it ([member data]): they aren't saved in the scene anymore. If [member data] is already set, it is saved to [param path] (like [method ResourceSaver.save]). In the editor, this is the [b]Save to File[/b] button of the Foliage tab of the Landscape dock.

method.name: set_foliage_type
method.description: Replaces the foliage type at [param index], keeping its instances.

method.name: set_instances_in_rect
method.description: Replaces the instances of the type [param type_index] in a rect of the landscape space by raw instances (see [method get_instances_in_rect]).

method.name: set_type_data
method.description: Replaces all the instances of the type [param type_index] by compressed data (see [method get_type_data]).

method.name: snap_to_terrain
method.description: Puts the instances in a rect of the landscape space (all of them when empty) back on the terrain.

members.member: If [code]false[/code], no level of detail casts shadows.
Size in meters of the cells (chunks) the instances are sorted into. Smaller cells are culled more precisely and switch levels of detail as a whole more often, at the cost of more draw calls.

The instances, when they aren't saved in the scene ([member instance_data]). A [LandscapeFoliageData] saved to a [code].lfdata[/code] file is streamed: only the cells needed around the camera and the streaming sources are loaded. Its layers are aligned with the foliage types (by index). Setting an empty data moves the instances of the node into it; setting a data that has instances replaces those of the node. Clearing it puts every instance back in the node. Edits are kept in memory until the data is saved (in the editor, with the scene).

Colors the instances for debugging and draws the bounds of the drawn cells (like [member Landscape3D.debug_view]). When the LOD of the landscape is frozen ([member Landscape3D.freeze_lod]), the foliage keeps its levels of detail too, so that they can be inspected from another point of view.
The foliage types of the instances. Use [method add_foliage_type], [method remove_foliage_type] and [method set_foliage_type] to change them while keeping the instances.
If [code]true[/code], instances are put back on the terrain (keeping their offset from the ground and adjusting their alignment) when the heights of the landscape change under them.

If [code]true[/code], the GPU culling removes the instances outside of the view frustum of each camera drawn (the bounding sphere of every instance is tested, just before the camera is drawn, so every viewport sees its own instances). While the level of detail of the landscape is frozen ([member Landscape3D.freeze_lod]), the last view of its camera is kept instead. Shadows are always drawn from every instance within the cull distance.

If [code]true[/code], the instances of the cells within the cull distance of the camera are uploaded to the GPU (only the modified cells are uploaded again), where a compute shader chooses the level of detail of each instance (with the same distances, cull distances and hysteresis as the CPU). Just before each camera is drawn, the instances are culled against its view frustum ([member gpu_frustum_culling]) and its occlusion buffer ([member gpu_occlusion_culling]), and the visible ones are written into one indirect [MultiMesh] per level of detail (and one per level for the shadows). This removes the draw calls per cell and the CPU work when the camera moves, which helps with dense foliage. Requires the Forward+ or Mobile renderer: otherwise the instances are culled on the CPU (see [method is_gpu_indirect_supported]). The debug views are supported ([constant DEBUG_VIEW_CELL_STATE] draws the instances in green).

The maximum number of instances drawn per level of detail of a foliage type with [member gpu_indirect] (the capacity of its indirect [MultiMesh]es, which adapts to the visible instances up to this limit). Instances beyond it aren't drawn (see [code]gpu_dropped[/code] in [method get_statistics]).

If [code]true[/code], the GPU culling removes the instances hidden behind other objects (the terrain, buildings, other foliage...) in the occlusion buffer of each camera drawn, with the same test as the renderer: requires [member Viewport.use_hzb_occlusion_culling] (or [member Viewport.use_occlusion_culling] with occluders) in the viewport, see [member ProjectSettings.rendering/occlusion_culling/use_hzb_occlusion_culling]. The bounding sphere of every instance is tested, so a single [MultiMesh] draws only the visible instances.
The instances of each foliage type, compressed (see [method get_type_data]).
Multiplies the level of detail and cull distances of all foliage types (e.g. a quality setting).
The render layers the foliage is drawn on.

If [code]true[/code], what the terrain of the landscape hides from the camera of the landscape (see [member Landscape3D.lod_camera_path]) isn't drawn: behind hills, down the other side of a ridge. Unlike the occlusion culling of the renderer with the depth buffer (HZB), which loses most of its effect when the camera moves, it relies on the horizon of the terrain seen from the camera, built again whenever it moves (about a millisecond on a few threads), and is exact for the current frame. With [member gpu_indirect], every instance is tested (in the views of the camera of the landscape); otherwise, the cells entirely hidden only draw their shadows. It is conservative: the terrain is taken at the lowest height of each patch of the landscape ([member Landscape3D.patch_size]), minus a margin for its level of detail and its micro detail, and holes don't hide anything, so what is visible is never culled. Ridges narrower than about two patches don't hide much. Disabled below the terrain (e.g. in caves) and with orthogonal cameras. Disable it when other cameras see the foliage at the same time (split screen), as it is computed for the camera of the landscape only (the GPU culling only applies it to the views of that camera).

constants.constant: Instances are colored by level of detail, with the colors of [constant Landscape3D.DEBUG_VIEW_LOD_LEVELS] (and of the LOD window of the editor). The bounds of the cells drawn as a whole have the color of their level, the bounds of the cells sorted per instance are white.
Instances and bounds are colored by cell (chunk).

Instances and bounds are colored by how their cell is drawn: blue when it is entirely within one level of detail and drawn as a whole, orange when it crosses a level of detail or cull distance and is sorted per instance (the cells whose updates would move to the GPU with indirect drawing).

Number of floats of an instance in the raw data of [method get_instances_in_rect]: the 3 x 4 transform in the layout of [MultiMesh] buffers, the offset from the ground, the random value and the alignment normal.
